verdict: Disney's revenue was flat at $22.5B — a record quarter at the parks (Experiences profit up 13% to $1.9B) offset an Entertainment segment whose profit fell 35% against last year's blockbuster slate; reported EPS rose to $0.73 mainly because a year ago carried $1.5B of restructuring charges.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairment charges
opex.note: Mostly a $450M writedown of Disney's stake in A+E Global Media, partly offset by other benefits.

follow100Note: Of the $6.42 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, about $0.58 belongs to noncontrolling partners — $5.85 is Disney shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: A record quarter at the parks
takeaways.text: Experiences — parks, resorts and cruises — set a fourth-quarter record, with operating income up 13% to $1.9B: international parks grew 25% on higher attendance and guest spending, and domestic parks grew 9% on more cruise days from the Disney Treasure. Full-year Experiences profit hit a record $10.0B.

takeaways.title: Entertainment had a tough comparison
takeaways.text: Entertainment operating income fell 35% to $691M: a year ago, Inside Out 2 and Deadpool & Wolverine set box-office records, and Star India still contributed before its move into a joint venture. Streaming was the bright spot — Direct-to-Consumer revenue rose 8% and its operating income rose to $352M, with 196 million Disney+ and Hulu subscriptions at quarter-end.

takeaways.title: Reported EPS nearly tripled — on comparisons
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS rose to $0.73 from $0.25, but mostly because last year's quarter absorbed $1.5B of restructuring and impairment charges versus $382M this year. Excluding such items, adjusted EPS actually slipped 3% to $1.11.

oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment charges were $382M — mainly a $450M writedown of Disney's equity stake in A+E Global Media, partly offset by $68M of other benefits. A year ago the same line was $1,543M, including goodwill, retail-asset and Star India charges.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $268M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $92M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns.
footerNote: Of the $1,443M of net income, $130M belongs to noncontrolling partners; $1,313M is attributable to Disney (the $0.73 EPS figure).
segmentNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $691M, Sports $911M, Experiences $1,878M (before corporate costs).
